submission.justification: Based on comprehensive simulation studies, Absorber-F1 with 4 mm plate thickness is recommended as it provides the best energy resolution while meeting all constraints. Among the viable candidates (F1 and F2), F1 achieves significantly better energy resolution at 100 GeV (3.816% vs 5.225% for F2), representing a 1.4 percentage point improvement. Absorber-F3, despite offering the best raw resolution (3.2% at 5mm), is disqualified due to exceeding the dose rate limit by more than 4x (85 μSv/h vs 20 μSv/h limit), making hands-on maintenance unsafe. The 4 mm thickness for F1 was determined through optimization across the allowed 2-10 mm range, showing the best performance compared to other thicknesses tested (2mm: 4.431%, 5mm: 3.9%, 6mm: 3.881%, 8mm: 4.607%, 10mm: 5.289%).

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F1 at 4mm achieves 3.816% resolution, which is the best among viable candidates. F2 at optimal thickness achieves only 5.225%. F3 is excluded due to dose constraint violation.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is one of the three candidate materials (F1, F2, F3) specified in the project documents.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 μSv/h
requirements.evidence: F1 has a dose rate of 12 μSv/h, which is below the 20 μSv/h limit. F2 also meets this at 6 μSv/h, but F3 fails at 85 μSv/h.
The recommended thickness of 4 mm falls within the specified range of 2-10 mm.
